gait.observation: Column 1 and column 3 repeatedly retain the same screen-side extended/raised foot arrangement rather than a readable opposite-leg half-cycle. Frontal row 3 clearly keeps the same viewer-left foot extended down and viewer-right foot raised in both endpoints; rear row 6 likewise does not swap its endpoint leg extension. E/SE/SW/NW/NE endpoints also look like repeated contact stances, with no convincing reversed near/far overlap. The useful opposite-stride cue from the corrected E2 pilot is not consistently preserved here.
gait.passing: Several middle poses lift a knee or tuck the feet, but that alone does not establish a complete alternating step when the endpoints repeat. Row 1's passing phase is particularly close to its contact phases.
gait.pixel_uniqueness: Unique rendering/shading pixels would not cure this anatomical failure; they are not counted as distinct support phases.

attachment_crop_and_spacing.body_attachment: No obvious extra limb or detached torso within individual visible figures, but adjacent figures touch in the atlas.

attachment_crop_and_spacing.gutter_failure: The middle-column figures in visual rows 3, 4 and 5 join into one connected component spanning y477..1192. Multiple adjacent rows nearly touch. The requested 12 percent safety margins and separated pose regions are not met.
attachment_crop_and_spacing.scale_consistency: Rear rows are visibly taller than upper rows: roughly 263-308px bodies versus about 234-249px in upper rows. Matching body/camera proportions require review, not automatic acceptance.
